مُعَقَّبٌ One who is made to go forth, (so in the CK,) or who goes forth, (O, and so in my MS. copy of the K,) from the shop of the vintner when a greater man than he enters. (O, K.) ―
-b2- جَآءَ مُعَقَّبًا He came at the end, or close, of the day. (TA.) ―
-b3- قِدْحٌ مُعَقَّبٌ An arrow which [in the game called المَيْسِر] is returned into the رِبَابَة [q. v.] time after time; the prize allotted to which is hoped for. (TA.) ―
-b4- جَزُورٌ سَحُوفُ المُعَقَّبِ A fat slaughtered camel. (TA.) ―
-b5- نَعْلٌ مُعَقَّبَةٌ A sandal having an عَقِب [q. v.]. (O, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
